{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABbH7H-Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhEtDVY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 122, "title": "Unify demo and local ROM selection behind a stable cartridge switcher", "body": "## Problem

The SNES emulator currently exposes two separate game-selection actions ("Try demo" and "Open ROM") plus a shared Play/Pause control. After the demo starts, the first action turns into "Pause demo"/"Resume demo", duplicating the toolbar Play/Pause. Selecting a local ROM only loads it and requires a second Play click. This is confusing and gives the bundled game excessive special treatment.

The maintainer requests one persistent **cartridge-slot** interaction instead: always show the currently inserted cartridge, and use a single "Change cartridge" control to choose either the bundled demo or a local ROM. Keep the layout stable before and after loading, and communicate the relationship through grouping and spacing rather than extra instructional prose.

Current implementation on `main` at `d6665e9965a40de7a637dc089a59224e6704692b`: [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), [web/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css).

## Expected outcome

Provide a stable, minimal cartridge interface for the general-purpose **snes-rust emulator**:

- A small, persistent **Inserted cartridge** label/value, showing "None" before loading, the bundled game's name when selected, or an appropriate local-ROM name.
- Exactly one nearby **Change cartridge** action, always in the same place. Activating it opens a compact accessible popover/dialog/bottom sheet with two choices: **Bundled demo — 潮鳴りの密室** and **Open local ROM…**. Dismissal changes nothing.
- Choosing either source **loads and starts emulation automatically** when validated ROM loading and save restoration succeed. No second Play click.
- Exactly **one Play/Pause** control in the common playback toolbar. The cartridge choice never becomes Pause demo or Resume demo. Reset, Sound and Fullscreen remain separate.
- The visible layout/position of the cartridge area and playback tools stays the same across empty, loading, playing, paused and error states. Status wording and the displayed cartridge name may change; controls should not jump or duplicate.

Use the three [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple**, **Show, don't tell**, **Intuitive and predictable**. Do not replace labels necessary for accessibility or safety with unlabeled icons.

## Context and implementation notes

The existing `loadCartridge(name, read, local)` path already implements ROM normalization, SHA-256 identity, validation, pause/save-before-switch, battery SRAM restore and error safeguards. Reuse it for both sources. The current local `#rom` change handler never calls `start()`, while the demo handler does. `updatePlayback()` currently changes the `#demo` button into "Pause demo" or "Resume demo" while independently updating `#play`: eliminate that conceptual duplication.

- Trigger Web Audio `AudioContext.resume()` as early as permitted by the initiating user gesture; the browser's file picker/asynchronous `File.arrayBuffer()` may cause user activation to expire, so handle audio-unlock failure gracefully with a concise retry/mute cue. **Video/gameplay must still auto-start** if browser sound is blocked; never autoplay the page merely because it loads.
- Replacing an inserted cartridge must honor both existing save-write failures and save-restore failures; keep the current cartridge and its recoverable SRAM intact when switching is blocked. Cancellation of the local file chooser or dismissing the cartridge menu must not pause/reset/reload the game.
- Selecting the already inserted **demo** must not silently restart it or double-load it. Prefer a no-op/return to gameplay; Reset remains the explicit restart control. Repeated activation and concurrent fetches must be safe.
- Preserve the single bundled ROM and its pinned hash/provenance, existing same-origin/CSP/Pages packaging, local-ROM privacy, emulator behavior, and no user-ROM uploads.
- Preserve touch inputs (all 12 SNES buttons), keyboard/gamepad, simultaneous presses, responsive portrait/landscape layouts, fullscreen, 256/512 framebuffer rendering and audio scheduling. The cartridge picker must not trap or interfere with touch-gamepad input after dismissal.
- No framework or extensive visual redesign. Prefer small, semantic markup and focused JS/CSS changes. Use a short menu title and two recognizable choices; avoid adding new paragraphs to explain the workflow.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] On desktop, narrow portrait and short landscape, the game screen remains the largest visual area and the **same compact cartridge slot + one Change cartridge trigger** stays visible/usable whether no ROM is loaded, a demo runs, a local ROM runs or playback is paused. No prominently separate Try demo/Open ROM controls remain.
- [ ] A keyboard and touch-accessible picker presents exactly two clear cartridge sources, has sensible focus/escape/outside-click dismissal, and cancellation leaves the current running cartridge/input/play state unchanged.
- [ ] Selecting the bundled demo from a clean browser fetches the pinned, same-origin ROM, validates its identity, restores SRAM, and produces actual emulated frames/input progression automatically. Selecting a local `.sfc`/`.smc` similarly auto-starts **without** an extra Play click.
- [ ] Playback has a **single** Play/Pause control with accurate current-state label. Opening and closing the picker does not pause playback. No "Pause demo"/"Resume demo" action remains. Reset explicitly restarts.
- [ ] Switching from demo to local ROM and back preserves per-ROM SRAM identity and restore behavior. Tests cover pending async loads, duplicate selection, failed fetch/invalid ROM, failed SRAM persistence/restore, user-cancelled file selection, recovery, and no accidental overwrite or loss of the existing game.
- [ ] Web Audio starts from a permissible user gesture where supported and reports a recoverable blocked-audio state otherwise; game video and controls continue. No audio is started merely by visiting the page.
- [ ] Real Chromium/Playwright integration tests exercise DOM state, playable bundled and local game paths, keyboard/touch controller input, menu dismissal, responsive layout and no 404/CSP/console errors. Verify 12 touch controls in portrait/landscape and no unwanted overflow or UI rearrangement.
- [ ] Keep the existing source-built Castle/Memory game tests, original diagnostic and hardware regressions, Pages artifact allowlist, local-file privacy and legal notices intact. Run and report relevant README validation, including formatting, warning-denying Clippy, Rust tests, production Wasm build and mandatory full Chromium suite, with any skipped checks clearly stated.
- [ ] Include actual desktop/portrait/landscape screenshots and a concise before/after workflow description in the PR/validation record; do not use concept mockups as implementation screenshots.

## Optional validation

Physical iOS Safari and Android Chrome, assistive technology, and subjective usability comparisons. Document observed platform-specific issues without treating them as blockers when all required pre-merge browser checks pass.

## Required post-merge verification

After merge, verify the new `main` GitHub Pages run and test the published app with both cartridge choices, auto-play and menu dismissal on desktop and mobile-sized viewports. Record the actual run/URL and results; this cannot block pre-merge approval. On failure, create a separate `task` Issue with evidence when invoked (no implied background monitoring).
